observation.visible_scene: First-person view riding down an escalator inside a brightly lit mall/food-court (caption overlay '新加坡裕廊坊香港街 2022'). Overhead hang neon signs (a vertical yellow/red Chinese sign, a green/red '紅珊瑚' sign, a yellow '新明星 牛扒之家' sign) and an orange 'POPULAR #B1-41' sign. Two parallel escalators flank the central one: on the left a masked man in a white T-shirt stands close to the camera, with a woman in a bun and a man in a black shirt leaning on the handrail further up; on the right a masked man leans over the railing looking down, with other shoppers behind him. At the bottom landing a person in a red shirt and beige trousers stands among lower-floor shop fronts. Glass balustrades on both sides reflect the scene.
visible_changes: The foreground masked man in the white T-shirt on the left slides out of frame within the first ~6 frames as the camera descends past him.

The red-shirted person at the bottom landing shifts and, in later frames, is no longer clearly visible (occluded by the lower balustrade / moves out of the sightline); a hanging rack of light-coloured clothing/bags that was previously hidden becomes visible at the bottom centre.

The woman at the top-left edge leaves the frame, while the man in the black shirt remains leaning on the left handrail, his position drifting slightly downward in frame; the masked man on the right keeps leaning on his railing throughout.

As the camera travels down, the overhead neon signs and the lower-floor shop fronts move upward in the frame and the bottom landing draws nearer, consistent with a downward camera translation along the escalator (not with the signs themselves moving).
A red figure seen on the left glass panel is a reflection of the red-shirted person, not a separate individual.
outside_clip_unknowns: Where the escalator ride begins and ends, and what the red-shirted person does after leaving view.
Whether the adjacent left escalator is moving up or down, and whether the white-shirted man was on the same or a neighbouring escalator.
Whether the bottom clothing display was revealed by the changing viewing angle or by an actual scene change.
uncertain_details: Exact gait/position of the red-shirted person (standing vs walking) is hard to confirm as the view is partly blocked.
Direction of travel of the people on the side escalators relative to the camera is inferred only from slow frame drift, not from clear step motion.
Minor camera tilt vs. pure translation is not fully separable from the background evidence.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
